item.title: ‘Bigger than internet’: Trump officially renames AI as ‘super intelligence’
item.description: US President Donald Trump has officially signed an executive order that replaces the term 'Artificial Intelligence' with 'Super Intelligence.' This shift mandates federal agencies to update their communications accordingly, showcasing the evolving technological landscape. At a White House gathering with tech executives, Trump emphasized this pivotal change, with a new legal definition expected to be proposed to Congress in the near future.
item.dc:creator: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA

item.title: India's League of Legends team returns to Asiad with Hangzhou lessons
item.description: Akshaj Shenoy returns to the Asian Games as captain of India's League of Legends team, three years after the side finished fifth in Hangzhou. Four players from that campaign return, joined by two Asian Games debutants. The group has since won in South Asia, competed against stronger regional opposition and joined S8UL. Now, against South Korea, Chinese Taipei and Hong Kong, they want to compete, not simply learn.
item.dc:creator: VINEET RAMAKRISHNAN

item.title: Mark Zuckerberg, Priscilla Chan donate $4 million to save 600-year-old Hawaii fishpond
item.description: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan have contributed $4 million for the preservation of Alakoko Fishpond in Hawaii. This historic site, which is over 600 years old, faced potential environmental degradation and development pressure. The donation helped acquire the property for long-term stewardship by the nonprofit Mālama Hulē‘ia. Their initiative supports education about traditional Hawaiian aquaculture and native ecosystems.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Nevada volunteers remove 120,125 pounds of waste from Truckee River watershed
item.description: On September 26, over 575 passionate volunteers dedicated their time to a significant cleanup effort in Nevada's Truckee River watershed. Their hard work resulted in the removal of an astounding 120,125 pounds of waste, which included both litter and invasive weeds. This collaborative initiative also focused on planting vegetation and enhancing storm drains, all aimed at safeguarding the local ecosystem.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: INDIA bloc to meet today to finalise plan for anti-SIR agitation
item.description: The INDIA bloc's opposition members are set to meet to formulate a plan of action against the Election Commission, centering on the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Notable leaders from Congress and TMC will attend, while DMK and AAP will be absent. This meeting follows a recent protest by Left party members at the EC headquarters demanding Kumar's resignation.

item.title: Baby hippo Bumpy rescued in Kenya finds new family at sanctuary
item.description: Five-month-old hippo Bumpy was rescued after being found beside his dead mother in Naivasha, Kenya, in May. Taken to the Sheldrick Wildlife Trust, he has grown attached to his keepers and formed friendships with another rescued hippo, buffaloes and an orphaned elephant. Bumpy will eventually return to the wilds of riverine Tsavo.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: Taylor Swift's former Beverly Hills estate where she wrote '1989' listed for $8M
item.description: Taylor Swift’s former Beverly Hills estate, where she wrote her hit album 1989, is back on the market for $7.995 million. The 1.5-acre Pillsbury Estate features a main residence, guest house, four bedrooms, five bathrooms, mature oak trees, a pickleball court and an eight-car motor court following extensive renovations by its current owners.

item.title: Delhi lecturer with cerebral palsy turns poet and disability inclusion advocate
item.description: Vinayana Khurana exemplifies resilience as she rises above the challenges posed by cerebral palsy to excel academically and serve as an educator. Her passionate advocacy for disability inclusion initiates essential dialogues around social reform. Through her varied literary contributions, she dismantles harmful stereotypes related to disability, reinforcing the critical need for accessible education. Her numerous awards reflect the significant mark she has left on society.
item.dc:creator: SHAILVEE TIWARI

item.title: NIA arrests 13 in JMB-linked terror conspiracy case after searches across 3 states
item.description: In a significant crackdown, the National Investigation Agency has detained 13 suspects in Assam, West Bengal, and Kerala associated with the terrorist group Jamaat ul Mujahideen Bangladesh (JMB). Following an extensive search operation, investigators confiscated several digital gadgets from the suspects. Earlier, Assam Police had made several arrests in connection with the probe, revealing efforts to radicalize youth and extend the group's reach within India.
item.dc:creator: BHARTI JAIN

item.title: Roger Federer’s $550M fortune: How did tennis greatness build his empire?
item.description: Roger Federer's financial story is a case study in how elite sporting success can translate into a long-term commercial career. His Uniqlo deal provided large guaranteed income, while his On investment gave him significant equity exposure. These ventures, along with Rolex, Mercedes-Benz, TEAM8 and the Laver Cup, helped Federer build a fortune that goes way beyond tennis.

item.description: The Congress Working Committee has called for the resignations of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Amit Shah. Rahul Gandhi highlighted concerns about electoral roll integrity and alleged vote manipulation during elections. The CWC meeting also emphasized the urgency of restoring deleted voter registrations. Members discussed the necessity of organizing public agitation to raise awareness about electoral issues.

item.title: 18 warships to be inducted in 2026, largest addition in a year in Navy’s history: Rajnath
item.description: During the Commanders' Conference 2026, defence minister Rajnath Singh emphasised the Indian Navy's impressive blue-water capabilities. He unveiled plans for essential upgrades and the arrival of new warships aimed at enhancing maritime surveillance. Singh lauded the Navy's commitment to protecting vital sea lanes that are crucial for India's economy and energy needs, while also recognizing its significant contributions towards women's empowerment and regional security.

item.title: Fort Kochi’s 300-year-old Koder House completely gutted in fire
item.description: Koder House, a significant heritage structure in Fort Kochi, suffered complete destruction due to a fire. This building, dating back to 1800s, was connected to the influential Koder family in the local Jewish community. Previously, it functioned as a boutique hotel and hosted cultural events related to Judaism. The incident has highlighted the urgent need for preserving historic buildings in the area.

item.title: Trade irony amid Trump threat: Why Russia is buying its own oil as fuel from India
item.description: The underlying issue is not Russia's access to crude oil but its ability to convert crude into usable fuels. Refinery outages and infrastructure disruptions have constrained domestic production, forcing Russia to import products such as gasoline. In terms of magnitude, Russia’s import volume of oil products is not colossal. However, Russia, formerly the world’s largest oil-product exporter, now faces additional logistical costs
item.dc:creator: SMRITI JAIN

item.title: With eye on New Zealand tour, BCCI to issue Ranji Trophy diktat
item.description: With India's tour of New Zealand set to begin on October 22, the mental preparations have already begun. Ahead of the bumper five T20I, five ODI and two Test series, the key members of the Test squad would be required to play domestic cricket to stay fit and match sharp.
item.dc:creator: SAHIL MALHOTRA

item.title: US to lend 40m barrel oil from strategic reserve as Ukraine war strains supply
item.description: The United States has proposed a loan of 40 million barrels of oil from its Strategic Petroleum Reserve to energy companies. This initiative is designed to counteract rising oil prices, which have been significantly impacted by the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran. As Indian refiners brace for a decline in Russian oil supplies, competition with China is pushing them toward pricier oil options.
item.dc:creator: PRANJAL PANDEY

item.title: Delhi bus gang rape: Charge sheet mentions semen, hair strands as key evidence
item.description: Delhi Police has charged a sleeper bus driver and conductor for allegedly gangraping a minor in August. The minor boarded the bus in Greater Noida believing it was heading to her destination. After the assault, she was dropped near Kashmere Gate, where she reported the incident. Forensic evidence collected from the bus includes semen samples and hair strands.
item.dc:creator: PRACHI KUMAWAT

item.title: 'No locus standi': India rejects Turkey president's remarks on Kashmir at UNGA
item.description: Ministry of External Affairs criticised Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan for raising the Kashmir issue at the UN. The MEA emphasized that no external party has a right to comment on India's territorial integrity. Erdogan suggested dialogue to resolve disputes, including the Kashmir issue, within the United Nations framework. India has consistently maintained that Jammu and Kashmir is an integral part of the nation.
item.dc:creator: ROHITASHWA RANJAN

item.title: INDIA bloc meet: Opposition to sharpen EC, BJP attack - what's on agenda
item.description: The INDIA bloc is gathering to address significant concerns regarding the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision process. This crucial meeting will see opposition parties deliberating on an agitation and a potential motion for the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Key opposition leaders will participate, although some, like the Aam Aadmi Party and DMK, will be absent.
item.dc:creator: ROHITASHWA RANJAN

item.title: How Russia's ballistic missiles, jet-powered drones have kept Ukraine under pressure
item.description: Reports indicate that Russia is intensifying its attacks on Ukraine, targeting key cities with ballistic missiles and drones. As Ukraine grapples with a lack of US-made Patriot missiles, the capability of its air defenses is being severely tested. Ukrainian officials claim that these strikes are a strategic move by Russia to weaken their defense.
item.dc:creator: PRANJAL PANDEY

item.title: FIFA hits back at UEFA: Infantino's lawyers accuse European body of 'harassment'
item.description: In a 21-page filing submitted late Monday (local time) to the US District Court for the Southern District of Florida, FIFA lawyers said UEFA was wrong to suggest that Infantino sought to personally profit from the project, which caused a backlash in July before being dropped within days.
item.dc:creator: SHUBHANSHU DWIVEDI

item.title: Watch: 2 girls, auto driver exchange blows on Bengaluru road over fare dispute
item.description: A video showing a fight between two girls and an auto driver in HSR Layout has gone viral online. The public video captures both sides exchanging blows until another girl intervened to stop the altercation. The police contacted the girls after the video circulated on social media, urging them to file a complaint. The auto driver alleged that he was assaulted after the girls refused to pay for their ride.
item.dc:creator: H M CHAITHANYA SWAMY

item.title: Essex farm flooded with seawater helped double saltmarsh across Thames estuary
item.description: In October 2002, a sea wall breach in Essex transformed farmland into a coastal wetland, increasing saltmarsh areas. This project, supported by various environmental organizations, aimed to restore natural habitats and manage coastal erosion. Marine life flourished, and biodiversity increased rapidly in the newly flooded areas after the breach. Traditional farming on higher land continued alongside saltmarsh restoration, contributing to sustainable agriculture.

item.title: Asian Games Medal Tally: How two gold medals lifted India back into the top 10
item.description: India secured two gold medals on Day 10 of the Asian Games, enhancing its overall medal tally to 53. Neeru Dhanda won India's first gold in women's trap shooting, setting an Asian Games record. The women's 4x400m relay team also clinched gold, adding to India's success in athletics. Additionally, India achieved multiple bronze medals in various events, showcasing its competitiveness.
